title: Dashboard & BI Design
interviewAnswer: A good dashboard starts from decisions and questions, not chart availability. Use stable metric definitions, clear filters/time windows, meaningful comparisons and enough context to distinguish signal from normal variation.
keyPoints: One screen should have a clear decision purpose.
Show denominators, time grain and targets/baselines.
Avoid mixing metric definitions across pages.
why: Dashboard & BI Design is a standard part of a broad data/ML curriculum because it changes how models are selected, evaluated or operated in real systems.
intuition: One screen should have a clear decision purpose.
deepDive: A good dashboard starts from decisions and questions, not chart availability. Use stable metric definitions, clear filters/time windows, meaningful comparisons and enough context to distinguish signal from normal variation. Show denominators, time grain and targets/baselines. Avoid mixing metric definitions across pages. A strong answer connects the formal idea to validation, data requirements and failure modes instead of treating the method as a recipe.
workedExample: An operations dashboard shows current failure rate, historical baseline, target, affected segments and alert threshold—not twenty unrelated charts.
commonMistakes: Choosing the technique without checking whether its assumptions match the problem.
Optimizing an offline metric without checking realistic validation slices or operational constraints.
followUps: When would you not use Dashboard & BI Design?
How would you validate or tune Dashboard & BI Design?
production: In production, validate on realistic slices, track latency/cost when relevant, and monitor for distribution changes or failure modes that the offline metric can hide.
